![](ship.mp4){#cr-ship .scale-to-cover alt="A ship sails in a polar region" loop="true"}

You can trigger a video to play using `[@cr-ship]{play-video="true"}`. [@cr-ship]{play-video="true"}

You can also pause it using `[@cr-ship]{pause-video="true"}`. [@cr-ship]{pause-video="true"}

Apply the `.scale-to-cover` class to videos to ensure that they fill up the whole Closeread sticky column (even if they need to be cropped to do it).

This is great for photojournalistic use cases like interviews where not every part of the frame needs to be visible.

::::

# Videos that progress on scroll

Let's use the popular `{gganimate}` and `{gapminder}` packages to generate a video (this demo comes from [the `{gganimate}` docs](https://gganimate.com)):

```{r}
#| label: build-ggani
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(gapminder)

gap_plot <- ggplot(gapminder, aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, size = pop, colour = country)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = country_colors) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 12)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~continent) +
  # Here comes the gganimate specific bits
  labs(title = 'Year: {frame_time}', x = 'GDP per capita', y = 'life expectancy') +
  transition_time(year) +
  ease_aes('linear')

anim_save("gapminder.mp4", gap_plot)
```

Let's incorporate `gapminder.mp4` into a scrolly section.

:::::{.cr-section}

Here's our gapminder video! It scrolls! [@cr-gapminder]{.scroll-video}

But wait, it seems to reset on our next trigger. [@cr-gapminder]{.scroll-video}

What's up with that? [@cr-gapminder]{.scroll-video}

![](gapminder.mp4){#cr-gapminder alt="A chart of annual national statistics, animating over the 20th century."}
:::::

\
\
\

You might notice that the scrolly video resets with each trigger. That's not ideal!

Most of the time, you're better off tying the scrolling video to a progress block:

\
\
\

:::::{.cr-section}

::::{.progress-block focus-on="cr-gapminder-prog" .scroll-video}

Here's our rayshader video again!

Notice that the video scrolls across several triggers...

... rather than resetting as each one passes.

::::

![](gapminder.mp4){#cr-gapminder-prog alt="A rotating landscape made with Rayrender."}
:::::
